claims.text: An ultra-thin ZrN interlayer between elemental Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate will impede elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Impeding Cr–Zr interdiffusion with a ZrN interlayer will prevent premature coating failure.
The ZrN-interlayer system will preserve protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The ZrN-interlayer system will preserve protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
Approximately 300°C represents the normal-operation condition relevant to the proposed coating system.
Steam exposure approaching approximately 900°C for transient durations represents the accident-relevant condition.
The proposed ZrN interlayer will be dense.
The proposed ZrN interlayer will remain thermally stable over the stated conditions.
A dense, thermally stable ZrN layer will moderate atomic diffusion across the Cr–Zr interface.
The ZrN layer will reduce the effective diffusion coefficient of chromium across the interface.
The ZrN layer will reduce the effective diffusion coefficient of zirconium across the interface.
ZrN suppresses Cr–Zr interdiffusion by acting as a physical barrier.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will maintain coating integrity during standard operation and high-temperature transients.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will maintain coating adhesion during standard operation and high-temperature transients.
Relative to a direct Cr-coated baseline, the ZrN-interlayer system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the baseline, the ZrN-interlayer system will form fewer deleterious intermetallic phases.
Relative to the baseline, the ZrN-interlayer system will retain protective functionality better under both stated operating conditions.
A Cr coating applied directly to zirconium alloy is prone to premature failure because of high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The ZrN intervention is expected to remain effective from approximately 300°C through approximately 900°C steam transients.
